children: ) said its open-source AI agent application, Harness, reached 1.54 million daily active users by Nov. 4, less than three months after launching. The company’s figures, disclosed Sunday on X, compare with roughly 271,000 users at September’s end and count people connecting to its servers.

For investors, the growth highlights competition shifting toward applications and developer ecosystems alongside AI model capabilities. DeepSeek’s reported computing usage also suggests wider adoption of autonomous agents could increase demand for processing capacity, while raising questions about operating costs.

image.alt: As of November 4, counting users on the official API, DeepSeek Harness has reached 1.54 million daily active users, consuming roughly 92 trillion tokens per day.

children: Harness handles tasks such as coding, file analysis and research with limited human supervision. DeepSeek is positioning the application as an open-source alternative to offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.

The startup plans a marketplace for developers to distribute plugins, which add functions to the application. A proposed developer support program would include AI usage credits, technical help and promotion, although further details weren’t disclosed.

DeepSeek reported approximately 92 trillion tokens processed daily, equivalent to roughly 60 million per active user. Tokens are units of information processed by AI models. Extended agent workflows can require repeated model calls, increasing computational demands.

The company said Harness has about 35,000 plugins and that 60% of users have created at least one, though their complexity varies. The figures reflect company disclosures rather than independently verified adoption or usage.

title: DeepSeek says agent app tops 1.5M daily users, plans plugin marketplace
